extracted.intended_audience: naval policymakers, DoD contracting/contract administration personnel, auditors, and researchers studying OMB Circular A-76 implementation and privatization
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and evaluation of the U.S. Navy's implementation of OMB Circular A-76, focusing on post-award costs, performance, and the accuracy/completeness of cost comparisons when functions are contracted out. Includes empirical measurement guidelines, recommended controls, and policy/training recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of pre-award cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The assumption that a pre-award bid to perform a particular function is an accurate estimate of the actual post-award cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether pre-award cost estimates reflect actual post-award expenditures; identify costs that are underestimated or not accounted for in the cost comparison process (the study examines how accurate pre-award estimates are for operations contracted out).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of unrecorded ('hidden') costs associated with contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there unrecorded costs associated with contracting out a supply operation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and enumerate costs not captured by formal accounting/management information systems; categorize such costs and determine their magnitude where possible (explicit research question driving the thesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude of unrecorded costs
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the magnitude of these unrecorded costs and what specifically are they?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify hidden costs where possible and list specific cost types (e.g., transition costs, administrative burden, damages, litigation, additional oversight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of hidden costs on activity, supported units, and major claimant
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the impact of these 'hidden' costs on the activity, the units it supports, and the activity's major claimant?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess operational, budgetary, and support-chain impacts of unrecorded costs on customers and claimants; include downstream effects on mission support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative significance of unrecorded cost types
rubrics_metrics.description: Which unrecorded costs are most significant?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank or prioritize identified hidden costs by magnitude and operational impact to identify which cost categories most affect net savings and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to minimize unrecorded costs (acquisition control, specifications, quality control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there ways to minimize these costs through acquisition control techniques, improved specification writing and/or quality control measures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate acquisition and contracting practices (PWS, Performance Requirements Summary, technical proposal processes) and propose controls or specification improvements to limit post-award costs and disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award performance effectiveness comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a significant difference in the post-award performance effectiveness of supply operations that have been contracted out and those which haven't?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure before-and-after performance metrics (quality, timeliness, accuracy, customer satisfaction) and analyze causes for performance differences where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant costs concept (incremental vs fully allocated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether in-house costs should be determined on an incremental or a fully allocated basis; adherence to principles of relevant costs in the CA program and cost comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cost accounting theory: incremental cost defined as the difference in total cost between alternatives; analyze whether the Navy adhered to relevant-cost principles when defining cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison methodology (full cost vs simplified incremental)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of methodology for cost comparisons: complex full cost computations versus a simpler incremental approach using standard cost factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand methodological changes (1983 move to incremental/standard factors), their implications for contested cost elements, and when full-cost detail is necessary versus standardized factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and accuracy of retirement cost factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The retirement cost factor used in cost comparisons is uncertain and has fluctuated (example: changes from 7% to 24.7% to 14.1% and later 27.05%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sensitivity of cost comparisons to the retirement factor and document policy changes and their budgetary implications; treat retirement rate as a contentious input requiring scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility and objectivity of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons may lack credibility when prepared by personnel who are unqualified or would be affected by the actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure qualified, independent personnel prepare cost comparisons; guard against conflicts of interest and provide oversight to increase trustworthiness of estimates (GAO finding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for periodic reassessment of contracted activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether OMB Circular A-76 requires cost comparisons to support contracting-out decisions or to reassess activities already contracted out to assure continued cost effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note GAO observation that A-76 does not generally require periodic cost comparisons for already-contracted activities; recommend policy or process changes if ongoing verification is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: CA program implementation phases
rubrics_metrics.description: The process consists of four phases: inventory, management review, cost comparison, and implementation of the results of the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow each phase: inventory to identify candidate commercial activities; management review to identify special circumstances; conduct cost comparison per guidance; implement results and track post-award performance and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance definition and measurement (use of proxies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance cannot be measured directly; proxies or surrogate measures are established and used as a means of assessing performance (risk that proxies don't reflect true quality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully select performance proxies, examine whether proxies align with desired outcome measures, and avoid measures that can be gamed or manipulated; consider multiple measures to capture quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability of Performance Requirements Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) used to assess contractor performance can become the focus for measurement manipulation (example: intensifying apple color without improving flavor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design PRS carefully to capture true service quality, include anti-gaming provisions, and monitor for unintended consequences where contractors optimize for measured criteria rather than true quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation identifying the need for centralized post-award guidance and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and promulgate clear post-award guidance to standardize monitoring, reporting, and handling of post-award costs and performance issues across commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for centralized claimant/field-level guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for increased claimant guidance at the field level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training and centralized instructions to claimant organizations at local commands to improve consistency in post-award administration and cost accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of cost accounting systems and post-award program controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of an adequate cost accounting system and post-award program controls was identified as an issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement or upgrade cost accounting systems that can capture incremental and post-award costs; establish program controls to monitor contract performance and expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration staffing levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for increased contract administration staffing to properly manage post-award administration and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess current staffing vs workload, allocate full-time contract administrators as needed, and account for their salary costs in program expense calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of budget flexibility after contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting out may create a problem with budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how fixed contract commitments affect local budget flexibility and contingency planning; incorporate potential loss of flexibility in decision analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type and method of procurement considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract type and method of procurement influence outcomes and are listed as an issue to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether sealed bid vs negotiated procurements, contract type (fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, multi-function umbrella contracts), and solicitation requirements affect cost, performance, and post-award risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: CA training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Training needs for personnel involved in the CA program (cost comparison preparation, contract administration, performance measurement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish CA-specific training curricula to improve accuracy of cost comparisons, contract administration, performance monitoring, and dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor performance criteria (questionnaire list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to judge contractor performance: Observation; Routine Command Performance indicators; Timeliness measures; Accuracy measures; Safety measures; Customer satisfaction measures; External inspection results; Internal audit results; Quality Assurance inspection results; Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a multi-faceted performance assessment including objective metrics, inspections, customer feedback, and internal/external audit results; document which criteria are used for each contract and track over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and warehousing performance metrics (T801)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific statistics for storage and warehousing functions: Receipt-to-stow on-time (%); Issues on-time (%); Warehouse refusals (%); Shipped on-time (%); Receipt accuracy (%); Issue accuracy (%); Ability to meet emergency requirements; General warehouse appearance (cleanliness); Local deliveries on-time; # Safety Violations; # Incoming Reports of Discrepancy (RODs); % Items Properly Packed for Shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect before-and-after contract award data on these metrics to evaluate contractor performance and service quality; use them for deductions, deficiency reports, and assessments of contract effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food service performance metrics (S713)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific statistics for food service operations: Sanitation inspection results; Equipment maintenance; Financial returns (over or under issue); Cycle menu development; Customer satisfaction indicators; Attendance levels; # Safety Violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track these indicators before and after contracting to judge whether contracted food services meet sanitary, operational, financial, and customer-satisfaction standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award administrative and transition costs often omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Common categories not fully captured by cost comparisons: Performance/quality considerations not accounted for; Administrative cost estimate is too low; Litigation costs; Transition costs exceeding assumed percentages; Costs for administering RIF procedures; Impact on productivity of remaining government workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include estimates for litigation, RIF administration, transition efforts, increased documentation and dispute handling, and productivity impacts when evaluating net savings of contracting out.

rubrics_metrics.name: CA program savings and calculation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: How program savings are computed: In-house retention savings (based on positions eliminated by MEO and computed for 3 years); Contract conversion savings (difference between in-house and contract bids) and MEO savings; use of NAVCOMP OP-73 cost-per-position figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute savings over the period covered by the cost comparison (typically 3 years), separate MEO savings from conversion savings, and document assumptions and sources (e.g., NAVCOMP OP-73).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program expense accounting (administrative positions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program expense defined as the salary costs of dedicated CA administrative positions (number of positions × $ per position for fiscal year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include program administrative salary costs when calculating net program savings (NAVCOMPT OP-08 Budget Exhibit figures used in the thesis example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey and contractor experience assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a pre-award survey was conducted and how contractor experience was assessed (references, previous Navy work, on-site visits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require and document pre-award surveys, evaluate contractor experience via references and past performance, and record who conducted the survey and what was done as part of procurement best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking contract modifications and PWS changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor whether the PWS (scope of work), deduction schedule, PRS, or procedures changed during the contract and whether changes affected contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records of all post-award changes, analyze reasons (scope, procedures, deductions, PRS), and include their cost impacts when measuring post-award outcomes and contractor performance.
